chunks: A man said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'No children are being born for me.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Seek forgiveness of your Lord during the pre-dawn time, one hundred times. And if you forget it, then fulfill it (make it up).'

key_terms.اسْتَغْفِرْ: istighfar — the act of seeking forgiveness from Allah; a core devotional practice in Islam
key_terms.السَّحَر: the pre-dawn period (sahar), approximately the last third of the night before Fajr, considered an especially blessed time for supplication
key_terms.فَاقْضِهِ: fulfill/make up (qada) — the same term used for making up missed obligatory acts like prayer, indicating the importance of consistency in this practice

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they are not having children according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith, a man complains to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about his inability to have children. The Imam prescribes a specific supplication practice: seeking forgiveness (istighfar) one hundred times during the pre-dawn hours (sahar), with provision for making it up if forgotten. This teaching draws on the Quranic connection between istighfar and the blessing of progeny, as noted in Surah Nuh (71:10-12), where the Prophet Nuh tells his people that seeking forgiveness will bring them children, increase their wealth, and send rain upon them.
